from.place: Proof paragraph 2 of prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint: derived coefficient adjunction, via the stable enhancement and finite pushout grid of lem-coef-suspension-square-comparison; local cone filling in the mapping-space universal property of pointwise Kan diagrams.

title: Relative pointwise Kan extensions exist from local universal cone lifts
statement:
Use [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. Let $\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal C$ be a full subcategory of a quasicategory. Let $p:\mathcal D\to\mathcal B$ be an isofibration of quasicategories: $p$ lifts all inner horns, and each equivalence in $\mathcal B$ with source $p(x)$ lifts to an equivalence with source $x$. Suppose $h:\mathcal A\to\mathcal D$ and $s:\mathcal C\to\mathcal B$ satisfy $ph=s|_{\mathcal A}$ exactly. For $c\in\mathcal C$ set $K_c=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal C}\mathcal C_{/c}$, with projection $a_c:K_c\to\mathcal A$ and canonical cocone $k_c:K_c^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal C$. Here the slice consists of simplices ending at $c$, projected by their entire initial face, and $k_c$ appends $c$.
If for every $c$ there is a $p$-colimit diagram $q_c:K_c^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal D$ satisfying $q_c|_{K_c}=ha_c$ and $pq_c=sk_c$, then there exists $H:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ with $H|_{\mathcal A}=h$ and $pH=s$ exactly. One may require $Hk_c$ to be a $p$-colimit diagram for every $c$.
The right-hand dual also holds: put $L_c=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal C}\mathcal C_{c/}$, projected by the entire final face, with canonical cone $l_c:L_c^{\triangleleft}\to\mathcal C$; the coslice consists of simplices starting at $c$. If every local lifting problem has a $p$-limit lift $q_c:L_c^{\triangleleft}\to\mathcal D$ restricting to $h$ and lying over $sl_c$, the same exact global lift exists, with $Hl_c$ a $p$-limit diagram for every $c$. All objects are in a fixed sufficiently large universe. Only these particular local cone lifts are assumed; no global completeness or cocompleteness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Kerodon Proposition 7.3.5.5, sufficiency, and its opposite dual; Definition 7.3.3.1 for relative pointwise Kan extension. Relative universal diagrams use the equivalent characterization of Proposition 7.1.6.19. Kerodon identifier, not Stacks tag; online source, not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Use the arrow-correspondence geometry of [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-join-geometry] for the full inclusion $\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal C$. Write $K$ for its arrows, $\pi:K\to\mathcal A$ for source, $u:K\to\mathcal C$ for target, and $J=K\star_{\mathcal C}\mathcal C$ for its relative join. That statement supplies the cocartesian fibration $u$, the map $S:J\to\mathcal C$, and the equivalences $\psi_c:K_c^{\mathrm{slice}}=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal C}\mathcal C_{/c}\to K_c^{\mathrm{fiber}}=u^{-1}(c)$. We distinguish these two models throughout; they are not identical simplicial sets. Put $f=h\pi$ and $g=sS$. Then $pf=ph\pi=s|_{\mathcal A}\pi=gi_K$, using the hypothesis $ph=s|_{\mathcal A}$ and $Si_K=\pi$. Thus $(f,g)$ is a commuting lifting problem on $K\subset J$.

source.place: Opening arrow-correspondence construction and lifting problem (7.27).

proof.text: Fix $c$. The base for the fiber cone is $gj_c=sSj_c$, and its boundary is $f|_{K_c^{\mathrm{fiber}}}$. Precomposing with $\psi_c^{\triangleright}$ gives base $sk_c$ and boundary $ha_c$, by the exact equations in [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-join-geometry]. The hypothesis supplies a $p$-colimit lift $q_c$ of this restricted problem. Apply the existence clause (2) of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence] with $e=\psi_c$: $p$ is an inner fibration because it is an isofibration, and both indices are quasicategories by the geometry statement. It produces a $p$-colimit lift on the fiber cone itself, with its original boundary and base exactly. This is a separate existence argument for each $c$; no compatibility choices between the $q_c$ are assumed.

source.place: Lifting problems (7.26) and (7.28); transfer along the slice diagonal equivalence.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-fiberwise-relative-join] to $u:K\to\mathcal C$, $p$, $f=h\pi$, and $g=sS$. Step 1 checks the commuting boundary problem, step 2 checks every fiber-cone hypothesis, and step 1 checks cocartesianness of $u$. The original hypotheses give the required isofibration $p$. Obtain $\bar H:J\to\mathcal D$ with $\bar H i_K=h\pi$ and $p\bar H=sS$ exactly, and with every $\bar H j_c$ a $p$-colimit diagram. Set $F=\bar H i_{\mathcal C}$, so $pF=s$. This assembles the local cones into a single coherent diagram; mere objectwise choices would not supply $F$.

source.place: Apply Proposition 7.3.4.7 and its fiber-cone characterization, Proposition 7.3.4.3.

proof.text: For $a\in\mathcal A$, the identity arrow $1_a$ is final in the fiber $K_a^{\mathrm{fiber}}$ by [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-join-geometry]. The edge at that object in $\bar H j_a$ is exactly $\bar H\beta_a:h(a)\to F(a)$. It is $p$-cocartesian by clause (3) of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence]. Its image under $p$ is $s(S\beta_a)=1_{s(a)}$, so the last assertion of that clause makes $\bar H\beta_a$ an equivalence. This holds for every vertex $a$. The coherent transformation $\eta=\bar H\beta:h\to F|_{\mathcal A}$ lies exactly over the constant transformation of $s|_{\mathcal A}$. Let $\mathcal A'\subseteq\mathcal C$ be the simplicial subset generated by $\mathcal A$ and all vertices of $\mathcal C$, and extend $\eta$ to $\eta':\Delta^1\times\mathcal A'\to\mathcal D$ by the degenerate edge $\Delta^1\to\Delta^0\xrightarrow{F(c)}\mathcal D$ at each vertex $c\notin\mathcal A$; these identity edges are equivalences, $\eta'|_{\{1\}\times\mathcal A'}=F|_{\mathcal A'}$ and $p\eta'=s\circ\operatorname{pr}$ on $\Delta^1\times\mathcal A'$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-equivalence-prism-extension] with $\epsilon=1$, the inner fibration $p$ (an isofibration lifts inner horns), $\mathcal A'\subseteq\mathcal C$ (which contains every vertex), $h_0=\eta'\cup F$ on $P_1=(\Delta^1\times\mathcal A')\amalg_{\{1\}\times\mathcal A'}(\{1\}\times\mathcal C)$ and $g=s\circ\operatorname{pr}_{\mathcal C}$. It gives $\theta:\Delta^1\times\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ extending $h_0$ with $p\theta=s\circ\operatorname{pr}_{\mathcal C}$ exactly; every vertex component of $\theta$ is a component of $\eta'$, hence an equivalence. Put $H=\theta|_{\{0\}\times\mathcal C}$. Then $H|_{\mathcal A}=h$, $pH=s$ exactly, and by the componentwise criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] $\theta:H\to F$ is a natural equivalence. This establishes the exact global lifting equations, including at all higher simplices of $\mathcal A$.

source.place: Identity-arrow finality, beta equivalence, and Corollary 4.4.5.9 (here via Proposition 4.4.5.8, 01NX, with all vertices prescribed) for exact restriction.

proof.text: We check the stronger pointwise conclusion, which does not follow just from $pF=s$. Fix $c$ and use $T_c^-=j_c\psi_c^{\triangleright}$, $T_c^+=i_{\mathcal C}k_c$, and $T_c$ from [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-join-geometry]. Step 3 makes $\bar H j_c$ a $p$-colimit; clause (2) of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence] makes its restriction $\bar H T_c^-$ a $p$-colimit as well. In $\bar H\gamma_c^+$ the base-vertex components are exactly the equivalences $\bar H\beta_a$ proved in step 4, and the apex component is the identity. In $\bar H\gamma_c^-$ the apex component is again the identity, and a base component comes from an arrow $1_a\to e$ in $K$ whose source projection is $1_a$. Since $\bar H i_K=h\pi$, its image is exactly $h(1_a)=1_{h(a)}$. Thus both transformations have equivalence components. By the componentwise-equivalence assertion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], they are equivalences of the whole coherent cone diagrams. Clause (1) of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence] therefore carries $p$-colimit universality across the zigzag $\bar H T_c^-\leftarrow\bar H T_c\to\bar H T_c^+=Fk_c$. Finally $\theta$ restricts to a natural equivalence $Hk_c\to Fk_c$, so the same invariance clause makes $Hk_c$ a $p$-colimit. This holds for every $c$ without identifying $T_c^-$ with $T_c^+$.

source.place: The two explicit gamma comparisons in the last half of Proposition 7.3.5.5, followed by invariance of relative universal diagrams.

proof.text: For the right-hand assertion apply steps 1-5 to the full inclusion $\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}\subseteq\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$, the isofibration $p^{\mathrm{op}}:\mathcal D^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}$, and $h^{\mathrm{op}},s^{\mathrm{op}}$. Clause (4) of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence] supplies both the isofibration hypothesis after reversal and the cone/mapping-space duality: the opposite of $\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal C}\mathcal C_{c/}$ is the slice index in $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$, and the assumed local $p$-limit lift becomes the required local $p^{\mathrm{op}}$-colimit lift. The resulting exact global lift, reversed once more, is $H:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ with precisely the original restriction and projection, since the order-reversal construction is involutive. Its canonical cones are $p$-limits by the same clause. This treats the dual under the prescribed right-pinched mapping-space convention, rather than silently replacing those spaces by homotopy-category hom sets.

source.place: Opposite-category dual of the sufficiency proof; relative universal-cone duality.

proof_origin.place: Expanded proof of Proposition 7.3.5.5 and its opposite dual; online source not archived in literature/. The relative-join geometry, fiber gluing, cone-equivalence calculus and equivalence prism extension are exposed as statement-only inputs.
